why_v3: The CP179 pilot refuted the v2 adapter with four diagnoses. CP180 fixed the measurement (contract-aware decode + capacity + receipted branch selection). CP181 fixed the objective: positive depth-advantage margin (equality no longer optimal), differentiable branch-diversity pressure with per-step cosine telemetry (the v2 adapter had collapsed virtual width), assistant-answer-v3 bridge parity between training and live execution, and held-out validation. CP182's tiny-checkpoint proof validated every surface and the strict identity contract accepts v3 bundles.

training.execution_shape_rationale: n_slots 4 and two branch roles MATCH the resident interactive profile — train under the shape the runtime actually executes; curriculum depth 4 exceeds the live 2-step profile so extra thought is trained to help

memory_safety.rule: live desktop app DOWN for the entire run; one 32B process maximum on the 64GB host

requirements: training_completion complete OR halt wall_clock with >= 200 steps
finite loss trail and finite holdout trail
strict v2 identity contract validates the bundle naming objective v3
holdout mean CE at final checkpoint not worse than 1.5x its minimum (overfitting guard)
mechanical_admission.on_failure: REFUTED-mechanics; no evaluation compute for the adapter

post_training_pilot.decode: contract-aware termination (CP180) with decode_max_tokens 768 uniformly across every arm
advance_only_if: adapter_vanilla has no material regression against base_vanilla
adapter-RLC branch scores are NOT all tied (virtual width alive)
ordinary-generation isolation exact; all identity receipts validate
post_training_pilot.negative_or_inconclusive_action: diagnose, revise training, preregister a fresh pilot; do not run or claim the confirmatory campaign

required_controls: externally held task and provider trust roots
signed zero-overlap contamination audit against exact training corpus (tools/produce_contamination_audit.py; trust root ~/.aura/trust/contamination_audit_ed25519_public.pem)
